question: Who was the last Mauryan king, killed by his Commander-in-Chief, leading to the establishment of the Shunga dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihadratha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brihadratha** was the last ruler of the Mauryan Empire, which was one of the most powerful empires in ancient Indian history.
 
• He was assassinated by his Commander-in-Chief, **Pushyamitra Shunga**, in 185 BCE during a military parade.
 
• This assassination marked the end of the Mauryan Empire and led to the establishment of the **Shunga dynasty**.
 
• The Shunga dynasty ruled parts of North and Central India and is known for its contributions to art and culture, particularly in promoting Buddhism and Hinduism.
 
• Brihadratha's reign is considered weak and marked the decline of the once-powerful Mauryan Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samprati**

 
 
• Samprati was a Mauryan ruler and the grandson of Emperor Ashoka.
 
• Known for his efforts in spreading Jainism, he is often compared to Ashoka for his religious contributions.
 
• He built numerous Jain temples and promoted the religion in the regions he ruled.
 
• Samprati's rule is remembered for its focus on religious tolerance and the propagation of Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Bindusara**
 
 
• Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya, was the second ruler of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He was known as "Amitraghata," meaning "Slayer of Enemies."
 
• Bindusara expanded the Mauryan Empire significantly, conquering several territories and ruling efficiently.
 
• He was the father of Emperor Ashoka, one of India's most famous rulers.
 
 
 
• **Dasharatha**
 
 
• Dasharatha was a Mauryan ruler and the grandson of Emperor Ashoka.
 
• He is believed to have succeeded Ashoka to the throne but was unable to maintain the empire's strength and unity.
 
• During his reign, there was a decline in the power and territory of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Dasharatha also played a role in continuing Ashoka's legacy of promoting Buddhism.
